label: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 7
knowledgePattern: Track signs and counterexamples in ordered real inequalities
solution:
I is false: a=−1,b=1 satisfy a<b, but 1/a3=−1<1=1/b3. The reciprocal cube has a break at zero, so decreasing on each branch does not establish the claimed global ordering.

II is false: a<b gives −a>−b, and base 3 preserves that order, so 3−a>3−b.

III is false: a=c=−2 and b=d=−1 satisfy its assumptions, but ac=4>1=bd.

For IV, all four numbers are negative. Multiplying a<b by c gives ac>bc; multiplying c<d by b gives bc>bd. Thus ac>bd. Only IV must hold. Answer H.

hints.title: Separate same-sign and cross-zero inputs
hints.body: For a proposed universal rule, check whether its domain can cross a denominator break or include different sign patterns.
hints.recap: A counterexample must obey every stated order and nonzero restriction.
hints.pitfall: Behaviour on one continuous branch does not automatically extend across a missing input.
hints.pause: Test the reciprocal claim using permitted inputs on either side of zero.

hints.title: Apply one order rule at a time
hints.body: For powers of 3, first compare the exponents. For products, record the sign of each multiplier before combining inequalities.
hints.recap: Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number reverses its direction.
hints.pitfall: Do not multiply two inequalities blindly when their entries may be negative.
hints.pause: Prove the claims that survive and give valid counterexamples to the others.
